recipes.name: Bacon-Roasted Chicken with Potatoes
ingredients_raw: salt and black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).

Wrap each chicken piece in a slice of bacon, trying to cover as much chicken as possible. Place wrapped chicken pieces in a 9x13-inch baking dish, season with salt and pepper and sprinkle onion over chicken. Push potatoes down into the spaces between chicken pieces and around the edge of the dish.
Combine chives, basil, garlic powder, adobo seasoning, and black pepper in a small bowl and sprinkle seasoning to taste over chicken and potatoes.
Bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour, until bacon is crisp and brown and potatoes are tender. Sprinkle with salt, if desired, and serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Bacon-Roasted Chicken with Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: Learn how to make this delicious bacon-wrapped chicken thigh and drumstick recipe that is baked with baby potatoes and a special seasoning mix.

video.description: Basil, savory adobo seasoning, and chives sprinkled over baby Dutch yellow potatoes, and nestled in next to bacon-wrapped drumsticks baked to perfection is quite a mix of rich ingredients. Roasted onion and herbs top this meal while it bakes to perfection!

review.reviewBody: I modify the recipe a bit, by putting the potatoes on a foil lined cookie sheet with a wire rack holding the chicken placed over the top. This allows the drippings to flavor the potatoes and chicken to crisp up on all sides.

Absolutely one of the best receipes that I have made with chicken. Read the review from Scorpio GG and added some cross-cut carrots to the other vegtables and put them in a foil lined granite 13x9x5 pan, sprayed with pam first. Added part of the seasoning mix to the veg's and placed a sprayed grid that fits this pan on top. I also used thick cut bacon to wrap my chicken thighs in, but let some of the chicken be seen. Placed the thighs on the rack and sprinkled with spice mix. It took about 75-80 minutes to get done. But OMG all the juices from the chicken pieces and bacon made the veg's taste absolutely ( TO DIE FOR ). THE BACON WAS CRISPY, BUT NOT OVERDONE. Thank you for this wonderful receipe.Clean up was so delightful, Nothing to clean up.

We love this recipe! One dish and done. The potatoes are the best part! So flavorful and delicious!!!! I pretty much follow the recipe except for the following. 1) used russet potatoes and just diced them up into cubes & coated with olive oil to keep moist while baking 2) I've used both chicken breast and thighs and either works great. 3) I lay the bacon on top and do not wrap under the chicken as the bacon doesn't get crispy and we like it crispy! 4) I use paprika instead of adobe seasoning. A regular rotation for us!!

This was pretty good; however I did make a few changes. Used 4 legs and 3 thighs. Cut the potatoes in cubes and tossed in olive oil. Used garlic and herb seasoning (lipton) on potatoes/onions and on chicken. Laid bacon on top of chicken instead of wrapping. Everyone enjoyed it so I plan to make again.

We liked it, but there is no way that 6 thighs & 6 drumsticks could fit in an 8x13 pan along with the potatoes. I used just 6 thighs and 5 small red potatoes, quartered, and that amount was plenty. Next time I will elevate the chicken due to the juices/drippings. Mine did not crisp & look like the picture. The taste was fantastic! Very easy.

This is great stuff as is, but I changed it up a bit, too! I wrapped two slices of bacon around each piece of chicken and cubed three potatoes. I transferred the chicken and potatoes to another glass pan at forty-five minutes and put it back in the oven for fifteen minutes. The bacon grease was poured in with the fresh green beans that were simmering. As I stated....great stuff!!!

THE BEST EVER!
Only thing I changed was used chicken 1/4's and left them together, so no room for the potatoes.
No adobo so made my own and used Smoked Paprika which was awesome with the other spices!
After chicken was done I took them out and left the onions, cut the potatoes up and put them in the sauce left over and coated them and every 15 min turned them for an hr and half till roasted nice and brown. :-) OMG the best ever!

This was spectacular and easy to cook. My husband really loved it. I used a chicken breast cut in half down the center, which took 2 strips of bacon per half to wrap. For the seasoning, I used salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and dill. Then, I drizzled olive oil over everything. I was only making 2 servings, so baked for 40 minutes at 400.

We loved it very tasty, I used chicken breast made my own adobo season ,layed bacon over chicken, russet potatoes, carrots,onion ,bell pepper, cooked @400 covered 30 minutes then uncovered for 30 , came out perfect!

This is my first recipe review, but thought this one was worthy! It was so easy! I used frozen chicken breast tenderloins straight out of the freezer. I cubed small golden potatoes, carrots and onions and placed on the bottom of a foil lined pan. I seasoned them with garlic powder, salt, pepper and adobo (never used adobo before tonight) and then placed chicken tenderloins on top and draped bacon slices on top of it all. It took right at an hour in a 400 degree oven. This saved me tonight! I had a house full of hungry teens and a late start to dinner. Nevertheless, I got a round of thank yous for the great meal. THAT is worth taking a few minutes to thank the other reviewers for these easy adaptations to this great recipe, and to throw in my agreement. Definitely worth making this one!

this was AMAZING! I didn't have Adobo so I just added paprika and ground oregano to the spice mixture, there was enough black pepper and garlic in it for us already. I used boneless, skinless thighs and 'crisped' them under the broiler for a minute before serving. Baby red potatoes was all I had, the gold potatoes may have made a prettier presentation but when a dish tastes this good, who cares!!!

I thought this was pretty good. I used 1 chicken breast, pounded to about 1/2 inch thickness and split into 2 portions. used 2 bacon strips per breast portion. I had a handful of small red potatoes that I quartered. I halved the seasoning but probably used about half of that over the chicken and potatoes. That was plenty. I baked it for 40 minutes, and probably should have only baked it for 35 minutes, but the bacon seemed to need a little more. I also should have lined my pan with aluminum foil or at least have sprayed it with cooking spray, because some of my potatoes stuck/burned to the sides. I might consider what some other reviewers suggested about using a grate for the chicken so it is over the potatoes. That way the bacon gets more done and the drippings flavor the potatoes. My hubby thought the chicken needed a drizzle of something either sweet or a little spicy. I will probably make this again and see how it works with a little extra saucy drizzle and the modifications mentioned above.

I used chicken breast tenderloins with cubed russet potatoes (both already on hand). Portion control made simple! Very tasty herb mix.
Tasty! Needed and extra 30 minutes in oven. Served with a crunchy kale salad.
Easy to make, delicious to eat! Made a few changes to the recipe but it will be easy to personalize each time it gets made.

If you have drumsticks to use up, this was good. I did use a rack in a foil lined sheet pan (putting the potatoes in the bottom). I do not typically buy dark meat, but these legs came in my Butcher Box.

Great way to add excitment to drumsticks.
Came out perfect. Cheap and tasty. The Fam loved it. 400 for 40min
